findings.title: Recovery codes stored in user storage are never consumed and can be reused indefinitely
findings.body: When the recovery-authn-codes credential lives in a user storage (the scenario this PR enables), `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().isValid(...)` delegates to the storage provider's `CredentialInputValidator.isValid`. Unlike the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider`, whose isValid() marks the matched code as used, there is no framework path that tells the storage to invalidate the used code, and the reference implementation added in this PR (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid`, which does a plain `anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`) demonstrates that the same recovery code passes validation again on every login. One-time use is a core security property of recovery codes. Either the framework needs a consumption/update callback for storages, or the storage SPI contract (and the test provider plus a reuse-rejection test) must require storages to invalidate used codes; as merged, a federated user's recovery code is effectively a permanent credential.

findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById() is called with a user-storage credential ID it cannot delete
findings.body: After successful validation, when `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` returns a federated credential and `allCodesUsed()` is true, the code calls `authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. That ID belongs to the user storage, not Keycloak's local credential store (for the test provider it is even regenerated fresh on every `getCredentials()` call via `createFromValues`, and may be null), and `CredentialInputUpdater` offers no delete-by-id for storages (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.disableCredentialType` ignores recovery-authn-codes entirely). Consequence: an exhausted federated recovery-code credential is never removed, the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is re-added on every login while the dead credential keeps `configuredFor` true, and passing an unresolvable/null ID risks an exception from the credential store inside the authentication flow.

findings.title: Regenerating recovery codes does not remove a pre-existing credential in the other store
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` either stores the new codes in the user storage (`userStorageCreated == true`) or in Keycloak's local DB, but never removes an existing recovery-authn-codes credential from the store it did not write to. A user who previously had recovery codes in the local DB (e.g. created before federation or while the storage did not support the type) keeps that old credential fully valid after regenerating: `credentialManager().isValid()` can still accept the old local codes, so regeneration fails to invalidate the previous code set. Additionally `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` prefers the federated credential while validation may succeed against the local one, so the UI can prompt with a code number from a different credential than the one actually consumed. Both stores should be reconciled (old credential deleted) when new codes are created.

findings.title: Optional.get() without presence check now depends on user-storage getCredentials() consistency
findings.body: The bean still calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` unconditionally, but the Optional now comes from `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()`, which requires the user storage to (a) implement `CredentialLookupProvider.getCredentials` and (b) return credential data in the exact `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` JSON schema. A storage that reports `isConfiguredFor(recovery-authn-codes) == true` (which is all `configuredFor()` checks) but returns no/foreign-format credential from `getCredentials()` — e.g. the raw code JSON that `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` stores in `credentialData` — will cause a `NoSuchElementException` or a Jackson parse failure while rendering the login page, turning a misconfigured storage into a 500 error. Handle the absent/malformed case explicitly instead of `.get()`.

findings.title: Extending the frozen 4.8.3 backwards-compatibility provider undermines the test's purpose
findings.body: The class javadoc states this provider was created with Keycloak 4.8.3 and that "Future Keycloak versions should work fine without a need to change the code of this provider" — its whole point is to verify current Keycloak against an unchanged, old provider. This PR substantially modifies it (adds recovery-authn-codes support to supportsCredentialType/updateCredential/isValid/isConfiguredFor, adds getCredentials), so the suite no longer exercises a genuinely legacy provider. Also, `getCredentials()` can NPE via `getMyUser(user)` returning null (the sibling methods `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` and `isConfiguredFor` guard against this), and on deserialization failure it silently drops the credential from the stream, making `getCredentials()` and `isConfiguredFor()` inconsistent for the same user.
